helpCenter.collection.headline: Keep what you have and what you want in one collection
helpCenter.collection.intro: A collection organizes resources around a series, creator, or collecting goal. It can include resources with local files and titles you do not own yet, so you can see what is missing before deciding how to acquire it.
helpCenter.collection.flow.title: From a collecting goal to local files
helpCenter.collection.flow.define.title: Define a goal
helpCenter.collection.flow.define.desc: Create a collection, such as “Complete this series”.
helpCenter.collection.flow.gather.title: Gather resources
helpCenter.collection.flow.gather.desc: Add resources manually, save criteria, or connect a subscription.
helpCenter.collection.flow.track.title: See the gaps
helpCenter.collection.flow.track.desc: Distinguish owned, acquiring, missing, and ignored resources.
helpCenter.collection.flow.acquire.title: Acquire as needed
helpCenter.collection.flow.acquire.desc: Try to obtain files when an acquisition lead and a usable workflow are available.
helpCenter.collection.card.title: Three key ideas
helpCenter.collection.card.membership.ti: Organize resources, keep files in place
helpCenter.collection.card.membership.de: A resource can belong to multiple collections. Membership does not move its files.
helpCenter.collection.card.criteria.desc: Saved criteria include matching resources from the whole library; subscriptions discover items in external lists.
helpCenter.collection.card.progress.desc: Resources count as owned when they have local files. Ignore unwanted items to exclude them from progress.
helpCenter.collection.boundary: Removing a resource only removes its membership; deleting a collection keeps resources and local files. To exclude a resource included by saved criteria, adjust those criteria.
helpCenter.collection.examples.title: Start with two scenarios
helpCenter.collection.examples.intro: Define what you want to collect, then choose manual curation or automatic inclusion.
helpCenter.collection.example.series.int: You have the first two titles and want to track the sequels you still need.
helpCenter.collection.example.series.ste: Create a collection, then add the existing resource records from the resource page.
Open the collection’s Resources tab and add a resource you do not own yet by title. No local file is required.
Review missing items and decide what to acquire
Use the Missing filter to review the gaps. Try acquiring missing resources when leads are available, or ignore items you do not intend to collect.
helpCenter.collection.example.series.res: Result: owned and wanted titles stay in one list. A title without an acquisition lead remains a record; it does not automatically become a download task.
helpCenter.collection.example.author.tit: Scenario 2: Automatically group a creator’s work
helpCenter.collection.example.author.int: Your resources already have a creator property, and you want to avoid adding every new work manually.
helpCenter.collection.example.author.ste: Prepare a property to filter on
Make sure the resources have a suitable creator property with consistent values.
Open Criteria in the collection, select the creator property and value, and save. The criteria apply to the entire library.
Review the matching resources. You can still manually add a work whose creator property has not been filled in.
helpCenter.collection.example.author.res: Result: matching resources are included automatically, while manually added resources remain. These criteria define membership; they are not a temporary search within the collection.
helpCenter.collection.comparison.title: Collections answer “What is this group still missing?”
helpCenter.collection.comparison.intro: These are comparisons between working methods. Collections can complement folders, notes, and download history.
helpCenter.collection.comparison.files.l: Titles without files have no place in the directory.
helpCenter.collection.comparison.files.b: Include wanted resources in the goal and see the gaps.
helpCenter.collection.comparison.checkli: Membership and ownership need to be kept in sync with your library.
Resource records drive collection progress; criteria and subscriptions can keep the list growing.
helpCenter.collection.comparison.downloa: Titles without tasks or links can be missed.
Record the collecting target first; acquisition leads and tasks can come later.
helpCenter.collection.comparison.tip: You do not need to reorganize disk folders to use collections. Start with a small goal, check the list and progress, then add criteria or subscriptions.
helpCenter.collection.concept.membership: Collections reference resources without copying their files.

A resource may have local files or may still be waiting to be acquired with only a title and other information. The same resource can belong to multiple collections.
Membership can come from manual additions, criteria applied to the whole library, or subscriptions. Multiple sources referring to the same resource do not require separate file copies.
Removing membership or deleting a collection keeps resources and files. A resource that still matches saved criteria remains included; change the criteria to exclude it.
Example: one title can belong to both “Works by this creator” and “Series to complete this year”. Deleting the latter collection does not remove the title from the former or delete its local files.
helpCenter.collection.concept.criteria.s: Saved criteria decide which library resources belong to a collection automatically.
helpCenter.collection.concept.criteria.l:
Criteria use the resource filter’s properties and condition expressions, but their purpose is automatic collection membership across the whole library.
Manually added resources are not removed just because they do not match. With no criteria, nothing is included by criteria; the whole library is not added.
Filtering a resource view is different from changing collection criteria. Do not use persistent membership criteria as a one-off search within a collection.
helpCenter.collection.concept.criteria.e: Example: “Creator = A” includes matching works from the library. A work you manually add before filling in its creator remains in the collection too.
helpCenter.collection.concept.progress.s: Progress reflects local ownership and excludes ignored items from the total.
helpCenter.collection.concept.progress.l:
Owned means a resource has local files; acquiring means an acquisition task is in progress; missing means it is neither owned nor being acquired. Ignoring a resource excludes it from the collecting goal without deleting it.
Collected percentage = non-ignored owned resources ÷ all non-ignored resources. Catalog information or a platform entry alone does not mean you have local files.
An empty collection shows “No resources”, and one with every item ignored shows “All resources ignored”. Neither means collecting is complete.
helpCenter.collection.concept.progress.e: Example: with 2 owned, 2 missing, and 1 ignored resource, progress is 2 ÷ 4 = 50%. Including the ignored item again changes the total.
